privacyMeta.title: Privacy Policy | HuddlePace Slack App
privacyMeta.description: How HuddlePace collects, uses, and protects data when you install the Slack app. Zero audio recording, zero transcripts, plain-language data practices.
privacyMeta.ogDescription: How HuddlePace collects, uses, and protects data when you install the Slack app.

privacyLead: HuddlePace does not record audio or store transcripts. We only retain the timestamps and agenda modules needed to run your meeting timers.
privacyS1Body: HuddlePace ("HuddlePace", "we", "us") is a Slack app operated by tBeltty. This policy explains what data we collect when you install and use HuddlePace inside your Slack workspace, why we collect it, and how you can control it. Installing HuddlePace means you accept the practices described here.
privacyS2Intro: Slack workspace data. When your workspace admin installs HuddlePace via "Add to Slack" (OAuth v2), Slack shares the following with us, scoped to the permissions you approve:
privacyS2Item1: Workspace/team ID and name, and the bot access token needed to post and update timer messages.
privacyS2Item2: Channel IDs where a session is scheduled or a Huddle is detected, so Vector can post and update the tracking card.
privacyS2Item3: User IDs of session organizers and assigned speakers, used only to verify who may start, transition, or conclude a session and to send them private DM reminders.
privacyS2Item4: Agenda structure you enter yourself: module names, percentage allocations, and total meeting duration.
privacyS2Support: Support data. If you use the "Help" widget on this site or contact support@huddlepace.com, we (via our support platform, the tBelt dashboard) collect the name, email address, and message content you choose to submit, solely to respond to your request.
privacyS2Technical: Technical data. This website does not store a language preference. The language is set by the page address (/es/ for Spanish). We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
privacyS3Body: HuddlePace does not request Huddle audio, does not record calls, does not generate transcripts, and does not read channel messages. We only process the slash commands and interactive buttons triggered directly by your team. This architectural constraint is built directly into our codebase.
privacyS4Item1: Operate core functionality: starting, tracking, and concluding timeboxed sessions, and posting progress updates to the right channel or thread.
privacyS4Item2: Enforce role-gated controls, so only assigned speakers or organizers can control a session.
privacyS4Item3: Generate the pacing reports and 30-day session history available to your workspace via /pace report and the App Home tab.
privacyS4Item4: Respond to support requests submitted through the Help widget or by email.
privacyS4NoAi: We do not send any workspace data to third-party LLMs or paid AI APIs. HuddlePace has zero external AI dependency.
privacyS5Intro: We do not sell your data. We share the minimum necessary with:
privacyS5Item1: Slack Technologies, LLC: the platform that transmits and receives our app's API calls. Slack's own privacy practices apply to your use of Slack itself.
privacyS5Item2: tBelt Dashboard: our support ticketing platform (operated by tBeltty). When you submit a support request, the name, email, and message you provide are processed there so a human can reply to you.
privacyS6Body: Workspace and session data is stored in a self-hosted database (SQLite via Prisma) that HuddlePace operates directly. It is never shared with third-party data warehouses or analytics platforms. OAuth access tokens are stored encrypted at rest. Session and agenda records are retained to power your 30-day pacing reports; you can request earlier deletion at any time (see Section 8). Uninstalling HuddlePace revokes our access token immediately; we delete the associated workspace record within 30 days of uninstallation.
privacyS7Body: All traffic between Slack and HuddlePace is verified using HMAC-SHA256 request signing. Each workspace's credentials are isolated from every other workspace (multi-tenant isolation), ensuring no workspace can access another's data, tokens, or session history.
privacyS8Body: You can uninstall HuddlePace from your Slack workspace at any time from Slack's App Management settings, which immediately revokes our access. To request a copy or deletion of your workspace's data ahead of the standard retention window, email support@huddlepace.com or use the Help widget on this site.
privacyS9Body: HuddlePace is a business productivity tool intended for use by Slack workspace members in a professional context. It is not directed at, and we do not knowingly collect data from, children under 16.
privacyS10Body: We may update this policy as HuddlePace evolves. Material changes will be reflected by updating the "Last updated" date above. Continued use of HuddlePace after a change constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.
privacyS11Body: Questions about this policy or your data? Reach us at support@huddlepace.com or via the Help widget in the corner of this page.

faq1A: HuddlePace is a Slack app that keeps Slack Huddles inside their agreed time. It posts a live progress bar in the Huddle thread, splits the session into agenda modules and nudges speakers privately.
faq2A: No. HuddlePace records 0% audio and stores no transcripts. It keeps only the timestamps and agenda modules it needs to run the timer.
faq3Q: How do I start a timed Huddle?
faq3A: Open the scheduler from the Schedule Meetup button in App Home, the Schedule Meetup shortcut, or by typing /pace in any channel. Set the exact date and time, choose a duration and split it into modules by percentage. HuddlePace starts the session when a Huddle begins within 20 minutes of that time, and the progress bar appears in the Huddle thread. You can also start it yourself from App Home or with /pace start.
faq4Q: Can I use it for a daily standup?
faq4A: Yes. A 15-minute standup can be split into context, updates and blockers, with a private alert to each speaker at the midpoint.
faq5Q: Can I save an agenda and reuse it?
faq5A: Yes. Tick Save as template in the schedule modal to keep the channel, speakers, duration and modules, then start the next session from that template in one click.

rtLead: A retro without time blocks spends the whole hour on the first complaint. This 20/50/30 split gives metrics, improvements and action items their own timer, and HuddlePace runs the clock inside your Slack Huddle.
rtMod1: Look at what the sprint produced: finished work, carry-over, cycle time and incidents. Facts come first, so the discussion starts from one shared picture.
rtMod2: Pick the two or three topics the team cares about most and work them properly. Thirty minutes covers a few topics well and ten topics badly.
rtMod3: Turn the discussion into commitments. Every item gets an owner and a date before this block ends.
rtSplitP: Here is how 60 minutes divide. Change the total in the modal and the minutes follow the percentages.
rtDer1H: The first topic eats the hour
rtDer1P: A visible bar tells the room how much of the block is left, so nobody has to be the person who interrupts.
rtDer2P: Twelve minutes is enough to read the numbers. Arguments about causes belong to the discussion block.
rtDer3H: Action items arrive in the last two minutes
rtDer3P: Giving them 30% of the time puts them on the clock instead of the leftovers.
rtDer4H: Everyone leaves with a different list
rtDer4P: The Huddle thread stays open, so the team can write the action items where everyone sees them.
